paragraphs: A learned optimizer is a neural network trained to update another model's parameters. Such optimizers could accelerate training, but learning from many tasks does not automatically make them reliable on unfamiliar ones. This paper investigates how their built-in preferences, or inductive biases, affect both stability and transfer to different training problems.

The authors examine optimization through dynamical systems: they study how repeated updates evolve over time. Starting with a noisy quadratic model, they characterize stability conditions using eigenvalues of the training dynamics. They then use those insights to introduce simple changes to a learned optimizer's architecture and the procedure used to train it across tasks.

Across the neural network training tasks studied, the resulting optimizer improves optimization performance and meta-training speed relative to the leading learned optimizer, with optimizer computational overhead matched. It also transfers to tasks substantially different from its meta-training tasks. The contribution connects analysis of a simplified optimization setting to practical design choices that improve the tested optimizer's behavior.
neurips-2022-a-closer-look-at-learned-op.tldr: Dynamical-systems analysis guides changes to a learned optimizer that improve its stability, training performance, and transfer to unfamiliar tasks.

paragraphs: Knowledge distillation trains a smaller student network using the outputs of a stronger teacher. Surprisingly, a teacher with better prediction accuracy does not necessarily produce a better student. This paper examines why increasing teacher quality can fail to improve teaching, and why conventional temperature adjustment does not resolve the capacity mismatch.

The authors separate distillation's effects into correct guidance, smooth regularization, and class discriminability. The third concerns differences among the probabilities assigned to incorrect classes. Those differences communicate how strongly each alternative relates to the target. Complex teachers tend to be overconfident, while conventional temperature scaling limits how distinctly these alternatives can be represented.

Asymmetric Temperature Scaling applies a higher temperature to the correct class and a lower temperature to incorrect classes. This increases variation among the incorrect-class probabilities, giving the student more differentiated information about alternatives. The paper supports the method with theoretical analysis and extensive experiments. Its central contribution is a targeted adjustment to the teaching signal, motivated by information that ordinary scaling can obscure.
neurips-2022-asymmetric-temperature-scal.tldr: Applying different temperatures to correct and incorrect classes helps stronger teachers provide more informative knowledge-distillation targets.

paragraphs: A lane detector trained on labeled simulation images must cope with different visual conditions when applied to real roads. Unsupervised domain adaptation addresses this by transferring learning from a labeled source to an unlabeled target. CARLANE provides a benchmark for studying this transfer in lane detection, an area with relatively few existing studies and publicly available datasets.

The benchmark covers three domains and contains 163,000 unique images, including 118,000 annotated images. MoLane and TuLane support single-target adaptation, while MuLane supports adaptation to multiple targets. This organization makes it possible to examine both transfer into one target domain and the broader challenge of handling several target domains.

The authors systematically evaluate baseline methods, including their own approach based on Prototypical Cross-domain Self-supervised Learning. The evaluated adaptation methods have high false-positive and false-negative rates compared with fully supervised baselines. These findings identify a substantial remaining performance gap. Public datasets, evaluated models, and implementations provide a shared basis for investigating that gap.
neurips-2022-carlane-a-lane-detection-be.tldr: CARLANE benchmarks simulation-to-real lane detection across multiple domains and reveals substantial errors relative to fully supervised methods.

paragraphs: The Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus tests whether an agent can solve unfamiliar procedural problems. Many tasks are easy for people but difficult for AI systems. This paper investigates language as a possible part of that gap: people can exchange flexible instructions, whereas computer systems often depend on a narrow set of precisely executable operations.

The authors introduce Language-complete ARC, or LARC, by asking human participants to explain task solutions to one another using language alone. The collection includes successful instructions for 88% of ARC tasks. They analyze these descriptions as natural programs: instructions that convey a procedure without necessarily following the rigid form of executable code.

Two distinctions emerge. Human instructions draw on a broad range of basic operations, and they use communication strategies that go beyond directly specifying executable steps. The authors demonstrate that these properties limit how fully current program synthesis methods can use LARC. The dataset and analysis therefore offer concrete guidance for designing synthesizers that better accommodate how people communicate procedures.
neurips-2022-communicating-natural-progr.tldr: LARC captures human instructions for ARC tasks and exposes ways natural-language procedures exceed the capabilities of current program synthesis methods.

paragraphs: Goal-conditioned reinforcement learning trains an agent to pursue different objectives using a goal supplied as input. A central difficulty is deciding how to express that goal. Directly using noisy, high-dimensional sensory observations can make learning difficult and can also hinder the agent's ability to pursue goals it has not encountered during training.

The proposed method, DGRL, learns compositional goal representations and then passes them through a discretization bottleneck. This produces a coarser description of the objective while retaining a structure in which components can be combined. The approach focuses on the goal representation as a way to make both training and generalization more manageable.

Experiments span maze environments and more complex robotic navigation and manipulation tasks, showing that discretizing goal-encoder outputs can work well in these settings. The paper also derives a bound on expected return for goals absent from training while allowing expressive combinations of goal components. Together, the empirical and theoretical results support discrete, compositional representations as a useful abstraction for this learning problem.
neurips-2022-discrete-compositional-repr.tldr: DGRL combines compositional goal representations with discretization to support learning and generalization in goal-conditioned reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: Artificial lights can create strong lens flares in nighttime photographs, damaging image quality and interfering with vision algorithms. Methods designed for daytime flare removal fail at night, where artificial lighting has distinctive brightness and spectral characteristics. Flare7K addresses the shortage of training data representing the varied flare patterns and image degradation found in these conditions.

The dataset is generated from observations and statistics of real nighttime flares. It contains 5,000 scattering-flare images across 25 types and 2,000 reflective-flare images across 10 types. These patterns can be randomly added to clean images, creating paired examples of corrupted and clean scenes for training image-restoration models.

Flare7K also supplies annotations for light sources, glare with shimmer, reflective flares, and streaks. Those labels support closer analysis of individual flare components alongside overall restoration quality. The reported experiments show that the dataset broadens the diversity of existing flare data and advances nighttime removal performance, with paired synthetic training data supporting effective restoration of real-world images.
neurips-2022-flare7k-a-phenomenological-.tldr: Flare7K supplies diverse, annotated nighttime flare patterns that can generate paired training data for restoring real photographs.

paragraphs: This paper develops a framework for approximate Bayesian inference directly over functions in an infinite-dimensional space. The aim is to obtain a variational posterior: a manageable distribution representing uncertainty about the function being learned. The framework leads to a method called Gaussian Wasserstein inference, or GWI.

GWI uses Wasserstein distance between Gaussian measures on the Hilbert space of square-integrable functions. This supplies a tractable optimization criterion for choosing the approximate posterior. The authors state that the approach avoids pathologies that arise in standard variational inference in function spaces, making the choice of inference criterion central to the method's design.

An application incorporates deep neural networks into GWI's variational parameterization. This brings their predictive capabilities together with principled uncertainty quantification analogous to that of Gaussian processes. The authors report state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets. The contribution thus combines a function-space inference framework with a practical way to use neural networks while representing uncertainty about their predictions.
neurips-2022-generalized-variational-inf.tldr: Gaussian Wasserstein inference combines tractable function-space Bayesian inference with neural-network prediction and principled uncertainty quantification.

paragraphs: Graph convolution networks have performed well in recommender systems, but their empirical success has outpaced understanding of their generalization. This paper develops a theoretical guarantee for GCN recommendation models in both inductive and transductive learning settings. It focuses particularly on the roles played by graph normalization and nonlinear activation.

The authors complement their analysis with extensive experiments examining those design choices. This connects a generalization bound to concrete components of recommendation models, providing a theoretical basis for investigating behavior that had largely been established through experiments. The bound also informs a proposed method for improving recommendation called Item Mixture, or IMix.

IMix addresses the difficulty of learning from discrete item data by mixing the embeddings of positive-negative item pairs. It thereby represents aspects of a discrete space continuously, using the learned vectors associated with items. The paper provides theoretical and empirical support for its effectiveness. Its contribution links analysis of GCN generalization to a specific strategy for enhancing the models.
neurips-2022-graph-convolution-network-b.tldr: Generalization analysis of GCN recommenders motivates IMix, which improves recommendation by mixing positive and negative item embeddings.

paragraphs: Radar's relatively long radio wavelengths support robust measurements in adverse weather, but radar perception research has lacked datasets comparable in size to camera and lidar collections. Existing radar datasets also often omit elevation measurements. That omission makes it difficult to infer three-dimensional object boxes from the available radar information.

K-Radar supplies 35,000 frames with power measurements across Doppler, range, azimuth, and elevation, together with annotated 3D boxes for road objects. Its scenes include fog, rain, and snow across urban roads, suburban roads, alleyways, and highways. Calibrated lidar, surround stereo cameras, and RTK-GPS provide additional measurements alongside the radar data.

The authors introduce radar-based detection networks and show that height information is crucial for 3D object detection in their study. Comparing a radar network with a similarly structured lidar network demonstrates greater radar robustness in adverse weather. The dataset therefore supports investigation of both elevation-aware detection and sensor performance under challenging conditions, with baseline networks providing a starting point for comparison.
neurips-2022-k-radar-4d-radar-object-det.tldr: K-Radar provides elevation-aware radar data and detection benchmarks that demonstrate the importance of height information and robustness in adverse weather.

paragraphs: This paper studies learning dynamical systems represented by stationary Markov chains with an invariant distribution. It works through the associated Koopman operator, a mathematical description of how functions of the system's state evolve. Although algorithms for reconstructing such operators already exist, the authors focus on connecting their estimation to statistical learning.

The framework learns from finite trajectories and restricts the operator to a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. Within that setting, the authors define a risk that gives rise to different estimators. They also link this risk to estimating the operator's spectral decomposition, connecting prediction-oriented estimation with the recovery of dynamical modes.

These connections motivate a reduced-rank operator regression estimator. The paper derives learning bounds for both independent observations and dependent data, using mixing coefficients to express the latter case. Numerical experiments on forecasting and mode decomposition support the analysis's suggestion that reduced-rank regression can be beneficial relative to other widely used estimators. The findings concern this specified class of dynamical systems and estimation framework.
neurips-2022-learning-dynamical-systems-.tldr: A statistical learning framework for Koopman operators motivates reduced-rank regression with learning bounds and promising forecasting and mode-decomposition results.

paragraphs: Off-policy evaluation estimates how a proposed decision policy would perform using data collected under another policy. This paper considers contextual bandits with continuous actions and deterministic target policies. Such policies matter when an application requires a specific decision, such as a treatment dosage and duration, but ordinary importance sampling is ill-posed in this setting.

The authors relax the target policy and reformulate evaluation as kernel-based estimation. A key choice is the metric determining how the kernel measures proximity between actions. They learn that metric to minimize overall mean squared error, deriving an analytic solution through an analysis of the estimator's bias and variance.

The method handles vector-valued actions and optimizes the metric, extending beyond prior approaches limited to scalar actions or kernel bandwidth selection. The authors establish consistency of their estimator and report substantially lower mean squared error than baseline evaluation methods across experiments in several domains. The contribution makes the geometry of nearby actions an explicit part of accurate policy evaluation.
neurips-2022-local-metric-learning-for-o.tldr: Learning a local kernel metric improves evaluation of deterministic policies with continuous, potentially multidimensional actions.

paragraphs: Large neural networks impose substantial training and inference costs, motivating compression for devices with limited resources. This paper proposes a compression approach for wide, fully connected deep networks using neural tangent kernel analysis and random matrix theory. The theoretical comparison centers on NTK matrices associated with different network models.

The result applies in a high-dimensional regime where both the number of data points and their dimensionality are large, under a Gaussian mixture model for the data. In that setting, the authors establish asymptotic spectral equivalence among NTK matrices for a broad family of networks. This equivalence provides the basis for the compression scheme.

The compressed network's weights and activations take only zero or signed unit values, up to scaling. The term lossless has a specific asymptotic meaning here: the compressed model yields the same limiting NTK as the dense, unquantized model. Experiments on synthetic and real-world data support the scheme's advantages. The theoretical claim therefore concerns kernel preservation under the stated assumptions, rather than exact identity of every finite network output.
neurips-2022-lossless-compression-of-dee.tldr: Under high-dimensional Gaussian-mixture assumptions, networks with ternary weights and activations can asymptotically preserve the neural tangent kernel of dense networks.

paragraphs: Nocturne is a two-dimensional driving simulator designed to study coordination among agents that cannot observe the entire scene. Its focus is inference about other agents and theory of mind in realistic multi-agent situations. Obstructed views preserve a key sensing constraint while avoiding the computational burden of processing camera images.

The simulator computes visible features using efficient intersection operations in a C++ back end and returns them in vectorized form. This enables more than 2,000 simulation steps per second. Open-source maps and trajectory data allow it to load and replay arbitrary scenes and trajectories from real-world driving records.

The authors benchmark reinforcement-learning and imitation-learning agents in this environment. These agents remain well below human coordination ability and depart substantially from expert trajectories. The result identifies coordination under partial observability as a challenge even when image rendering and visual feature extraction are removed from the learning problem. Nocturne offers an efficient environment for investigating that challenge using scenes grounded in real driving data.
neurips-2022-nocturne-a-scalable-driving.tldr: Nocturne efficiently simulates partially observed driving scenes and exposes substantial coordination gaps in reinforcement-learning and imitation-learning agents.

paragraphs: Gradient-based meta-learning aims to prepare a model so it can adapt quickly from a small number of examples. This paper targets the speed of that adaptation. Inspired by preconditioning, it changes the optimization formulation to encourage a parameter space that is better suited to gradient updates, without adding extra parameters.

The authors recast the problem as nonlinear least squares. They use condition number and local curvature to actively enforce better conditioning in the meta-learning model. These quantities describe the local geometry of optimization, so the method addresses how readily adaptation steps can make progress through the parameter space.

Across several few-shot classification tasks, the proposed approach significantly outperforms its unconstrained counterpart, particularly during the first adaptation steps. Overall results are comparable or better as well. Stronger early adaptation creates the possibility of choosing the number of updates dynamically at inference time. The reported benefit is thus faster useful adaptation alongside maintained or improved final performance in the evaluated tasks.
neurips-2022-on-enforcing-better-conditi.tldr: Reformulating meta-learning as nonlinear least squares improves conditioning and accelerates few-shot adaptation without adding parameters.

paragraphs: Adding noise to stochastic gradient descent is a widely used way to train on sensitive data, but understanding the resulting privacy loss remains a theoretical challenge. This paper analyzes smooth convex losses over a bounded domain. For a broad range of parameters, it characterizes differential privacy up to a constant factor.

The result changes the qualitative picture of how privacy depends on training duration in this setting. Earlier analyses predict privacy loss that grows indefinitely with the number of iterations. The authors show instead that, after a short burn-in period, continuing to run the algorithm leaks no further privacy. The stated setting and parameter range are central to this conclusion.

The analysis combines privacy amplification through iteration, using optimal transport, with privacy amplification through sampling via the sampled Gaussian mechanism. This differs from approaches relying on fast mixing. The authors also state that their techniques extend readily to other settings. The main contribution is a sharper account of privacy over time for the specified noisy optimization problem.
neurips-2022-privacy-of-noisy-stochastic.tldr: For smooth convex losses on a bounded domain and a broad parameter range, noisy SGD's privacy loss stops increasing after a short burn-in.

paragraphs: This paper develops quasi-Newton methods for saddle-point problems that are strongly convex in one set of variables and strongly concave in another. These problems require handling opposing curvature directions. The authors adapt curvature-based optimization to that structure and provide explicit rates describing convergence near a solution.

The proposed random Broyden-family updates estimate the square of the indefinite Hessian matrix. This design differs from classical quasi-Newton methods for convex optimization. Their local convergence rate is superlinear, with dependence on the problem dimension, condition number, and an exponent that grows quadratically with the iteration count. The locality of the guarantee means it describes behavior near the saddle point.

The paper also presents BFGS-type and SR1-type variants with faster local rates whose displayed convergence factors depend on dimension rather than the condition number. Numerical experiments show that the proposed algorithms outperform classical first-order methods. The contribution combines a curvature approximation tailored to saddle-point structure with explicit local guarantees and supporting experimental results.
neurips-2022-quasi-newton-methods-for-sa.tldr: Quasi-Newton updates based on the squared Hessian achieve explicit local superlinear convergence for strongly convex–strongly concave saddle-point problems.

paragraphs: Cameras offer a potentially low-cost, noninvasive way to measure physiological signals such as cardiac and respiratory activity. Developing these methods requires data covering different lighting, movements, environments, and physiological states. Collecting that variety with accurate reference measurements is expensive and laborious, motivating a synthetic source of training examples.

SCAMPS contains 2,800 synthetic videos totaling 1.68 million frames. Each video is aligned with cardiac and respiratory signals and facial action intensities. The RGB images come with segmentation maps and detailed waveform information, including inter-beat intervals, heart rate variability, and pulse arrival time. These paired resources connect visible appearance to the underlying simulated physiology.

Synthetic generation provides precise synchronization, noise-free labels, and control over dataset variation. It can also supply labels, such as exact pixel segmentation, that are difficult to obtain otherwise. The authors train baseline models on SCAMPS and test them on real-world datasets to illustrate generalizability. This evaluation examines whether the controlled synthetic data can support physiological measurement beyond the generated videos themselves.
neurips-2022-scamps-synthetics-for-camer.tldr: SCAMPS provides precisely labeled synthetic videos for learning camera-based physiological measurement, with baseline tests demonstrating transfer to real-world datasets.

paragraphs: Time-series pretraining can transfer poorly when the target domain has different dynamics, trends, or cycles. Domain adaptation often needs examples from the target, which may be unavailable during pretraining. This paper proposes time-frequency consistency as a way to learn representations intended to accommodate unseen target domains with different temporal behavior.

The idea is to place the time-based neighborhood of an example near its frequency-based neighborhood in the learned representation space. The model has separate time and frequency components, each trained through contrastive estimation. Distances between the components provide an additional self-supervised signal, encouraging the two views of a signal to remain consistent.

Evaluation covers eight datasets spanning electrodiagnostic testing, activity recognition, mechanical faults, and physical status monitoring. Against eight state-of-the-art methods, the authors report average improvements of 15.4% in F1 for one-to-one transfer and 8.4% in precision for one-to-many transfer. These results support the approach across varied tested transfers, including using a shared pretraining source for substantially different downstream tasks.
neurips-2022-self-supervised-contrastive.tldr: Aligning time-based and frequency-based representations improves time-series pretraining transfer across the evaluated downstream domains.

paragraphs: Estimating depth from surround-view cameras requires combining information from several perspectives. This paper creates a shared three-dimensional representation by extracting image features from each view and fusing them into a common voxel space. The resulting volume brings the cameras' information together before producing a depth map for each view.

To obtain a depth map, the method projects the volumetric features into the desired image coordinates. Because each voxel carries local 3D information, the same representation can also synthesize depth at arbitrarily rotated viewpoints. Assuming the cameras' relative positions and orientations remain fixed, the method additionally estimates a canonical camera motion from the volume.

The approach uses spatial and temporal context to learn metric-scale depth and canonical motion through self-supervision. On DDAD and nuScenes, it outperforms prior methods, particularly in metric-scale depth accuracy and consistency between neighboring views. The shared volume therefore supports both improved individual depth estimates and agreement across cameras, with the fixed-extrinsics assumption underpinning the proposed motion estimation.
neurips-2022-self-supervised-surround-vi.tldr: Fusing surround-view image features into a shared 3D volume improves self-supervised metric depth and consistency between neighboring camera views.

paragraphs: Language models can perform well on natural-language tasks while still struggling with quantitative questions in mathematics, science, and engineering. This paper introduces Minerva to address that gap. The model begins with general natural-language pretraining and then receives further training on technical content, focusing the investigation on quantitative problem solving.

The authors evaluate Minerva across several settings and report strong performance, including state-of-the-art results on the MATH dataset. This shows that the resulting model performs well on an established mathematics evaluation. The paper also broadens assessment beyond that dataset to questions drawn from undergraduate scientific subjects.

That broader evaluation contains more than two hundred problems in physics, biology, chemistry, economics, and other sciences requiring quantitative reasoning. Minerva correctly answers nearly a quarter of them. This result demonstrates an ability to solve some demanding problems across disciplines while also showing substantial remaining difficulty on that collection. The two evaluations together assess both mathematical benchmark performance and a wider range of technical questions.
neurips-2022-solving-quantitative-reason.tldr: Minerva extends language-model training with technical content, achieving strong mathematics results and solving nearly a quarter of a broader undergraduate science problem set.

paragraphs: Knowledge distillation improves a small object detector by transferring information from a larger teacher. Many methods align intermediate feature maps by minimizing a distance between corresponding activations. This paper changes that comparison, arguing that treating feature locations independently misses contrast and structural information within the maps.

The proposed method replaces the usual pixel-wise norm with structural similarity, or SSIM. This makes the training guidance sensitive to additional relationships in the feature maps, preserving more of the teacher's intermediate information. The change is straightforward to implement and adds only a small amount of computational overhead.

Experiments on MSCOCO show effectiveness across multiple architectures and training schemes. The method significantly outperforms standard norm-based comparisons and also exceeds more complex distillation methods that use attention-based sampling. A reported Faster R-CNN R-50 result improves by 3.5 AP over a vanilla model. These findings indicate that changing how teacher and student features are compared can materially improve distillation without requiring a complex additional mechanism.
neurips-2022-structural-knowledge-distil.tldr: Using structural similarity to match teacher and student features improves object-detection distillation with little computational overhead.

paragraphs: Theseus is an open-source PyTorch library for differentiable nonlinear least-squares optimization. It provides reusable optimization components for end-to-end structured learning in robotics and vision. The paper addresses a practical problem: existing implementations are often tied to particular applications and do not consistently include features needed for efficient computation.

Several example applications use the same underlying components, including second-order optimizers, standard cost functions, and Lie groups. This shared foundation illustrates the library's application-independent design. Differentiability makes the optimization procedure part of the learning system, and Theseus supports gradient computation through implicit differentiation and direct loss minimization.

For computational efficiency, the library includes sparse solvers, automatic vectorization, batching, and GPU acceleration. Extensive evaluations across a set of applications demonstrate significant efficiency gains and improved scalability when these features are incorporated. The contribution is therefore both a common implementation framework and evidence that integrating these computational capabilities helps structured learning applications run more efficiently.
neurips-2022-theseus-a-library-for-diffe.tldr: Theseus provides reusable differentiable nonlinear optimization in PyTorch, with efficiency features that improve performance and scalability in evaluated applications.

paragraphs: The paper studies continuous-time systems governed by linear stochastic differential equations when their drift matrices are unknown. Choosing actions requires learning the dynamics while controlling the system. This creates an exploration-versus-exploitation problem in which maintaining stability is a fundamental concern, and conventional discrete-time analysis does not directly apply.

The authors establish that Thompson sampling learns effective actions with regret growing only as the square root of time and stabilizes the system within a short period. Their analysis characterizes an optimality manifold linking the local geometry of drift parameters to optimal control. This provides a way to connect parameter uncertainty with the decisions it affects.

Simulations using real matrices support the theoretical results. They also show substantially improved worst-case regret relative to state-of-the-art algorithms in the tested comparisons. The authors interpret this as suggesting that Thompson sampling explores more cautiously. The contribution combines a learning-rate guarantee with stabilization analysis for diffusion-process control, while the guarded-exploration interpretation remains an empirical suggestion.
neurips-2022-thompson-sampling-efficient.tldr: Thompson sampling achieves square-root-of-time regret and rapid stabilization when learning to control the studied linear diffusion processes.

paragraphs: When AI advises a person, the final outcome depends on how that person uses the advice. Confidence displays can influence this decision. This paper offers an initial exploration suggesting that presenting greater confidence than a model actually has can improve human-AI performance, even when the original model is well calibrated.

The authors first train a model of how people incorporate AI advice, using thousands of human-AI interactions. They then use that model to estimate transformations of displayed prediction confidence that could improve the human's final prediction. The optimization therefore explicitly considers the person's response to the advice, including the confidence attached to it.

Experiments involve hundreds of participants across four tasks using images, text, and tabular data, with additional simulation analysis supporting the findings. Performance is assessed through the accuracy and confidence of the human's final prediction. The results suggest benefits from optimizing the combined human-AI system. They support a possibility demonstrated in the studied settings, rather than a universal claim that inflated confidence improves decisions.
neurips-2022-uncalibrated-models-can-imp.tldr: An initial study finds that adjusting displayed AI confidence upward can improve human-AI outcomes when the adjustment accounts for how people use advice.

paragraphs: Semi-supervised learning uses unlabeled data alongside a limited labeled set to improve generalization. Its common evaluation protocols have concentrated on computer vision and often trained networks from scratch. USB addresses both the narrow task coverage and the computational expense by providing a unified classification benchmark spanning several kinds of data.

The benchmark includes 15 tasks from computer vision, natural-language processing, and audio. The authors systematically evaluate leading semi-supervised methods and release a modular, extensible codebase for fair comparisons. They also provide pretrained versions of state-of-the-art vision models, making further tuning more affordable and reducing reliance on expensive training from scratch.

The reported FixMatch evaluation takes 39 GPU days across USB's 15 tasks on a single NVIDIA V100. The comparison with TorchSSL requires 335 GPU days across five vision tasks, including 279 days for the four datasets other than ImageNet. This illustrates broader evaluation coverage at lower reported cost, making cross-domain assessment of a single algorithm more practical.
neurips-2022-usb-a-unified-semi-supervis.tldr: USB evaluates semi-supervised classification across vision, language, and audio while reducing the reported computational cost of broad benchmarking.
